![A group chat with a Pinned tab, beside a thread with Also send to the chat ticked](/lp/guide/en/blog-pins.webp)

The team argued it out in a thread, twenty replies deep, and decided: the new header ships on Thursday. The people in the thread know. Everyone else in the chat saw a message with a reply count and moved on.

## Why it is hard

Threads keep a chat calm, which is why a decision can hide in one. And in a busy chat, even a message in the open scrolls away. A week later someone asks for the link, the date or the rule, and a person who remembers has to stop and find it.

## How Genos helps

Two small things cover the two cases.

When you reply in a thread, tick **Also send to …** under the message box. Your reply stays in the thread and also appears in the chat, with a link back that opens the discussion. It is one message, so an edit or a reaction shows in both places.

For what people will need again, open the message's "…" menu and choose **Pin for everyone**. The chat then has a **Pinned** tab beside **Messages**. Click a pinned message there to jump to it.

```flow
Decide in the thread
Also send it to the chat
Pin a message written in the chat
Find it in the Pinned tab
```

## What you get

- **People outside the thread hear the outcome**, without reading the whole argument.
- **The context is one click away** for the person who wants to know why.
- **A short shelf for the chat:** the meeting link, the release date, the way you name things.
- **Fewer repeat questions.** "Where was that again?" has a place to be answered.

Anyone in the chat can pin and unpin, and a chat holds up to 50 pins, so unpin what is out of date. Pins are shared. To keep a message just for yourself, use **Flag for later**. On a plan that keeps less chat history, older pinned messages are out of reach too.

**Also send to …** works in direct messages, group chats and multi-person DMs, not in project chats. Tick it before you send: it cannot be added afterwards. A thread reply cannot be pinned, and that includes one also sent to the chat, because it is the same message. To pin a decision, write it in the chat itself.

## How to start

1. Open the chat where people ask the same thing twice.
2. Pin the message that answers it. If the answer is buried in a thread, write it in the chat first.
3. Next time a thread reaches a decision, write it in one sentence and tick **Also send to …** before you send.

One clear sentence in the chat beats a long thread nobody opens.
